validation: Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved ice-cream so much. One day, he saw an ancient ice-cream truck. The truck was very old and slow, but it had a big sign that said "Ice-Cream". Tim went to the truck and said, "Hi, can I have ice-cream, please?" The ice-cream man looked at him and said, "Sure, little boy. Here you go." Tim took the ice-cream and started to eat it. But it did not taste good at all. It tasted very bad. Tim screamed, "Yuck! This ice-cream is bad!" The ice-cream man just laughed and said, "I am sorry, little boy. The ice-cream is too old." Tim was very sad and walked away. He did not get to enjoy his ice-cream that day.
training: Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved ice cream and always bought it from the ice cream truck. One day, Timmy noticed that the ice cream was not as cold as usual. He asked the ice cream man, "Why is the ice cream not cold today?" The ice cream man replied, "I am testing a new cooler today. It's not as good as my old one." Timmy thought it was not fair for the ice cream man to sell warm ice cream. He asked the ice cream man to give him a cold ice cream from the old cooler. The ice cream man agreed and gave Timmy a cold ice cream. Timmy was happy and said, "Thank you, Mr. Ice Cream Man!" The ice cream man smiled and said, "You're welcome, Timmy. I will make sure to use the old cooler from now on." And they both enjoyed their ice cream together.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia had a magic lamp. The lamp was very special. It could grow big and small. Mia loved her lamp very much. One day, a foolish boy named Tom saw Mia's lamp. He wanted the lamp for himself. Tom tried to take the lamp away from Mia. Mia was sad and asked Tom to give her lamp back. Tom saw how much Mia loved her lamp. He felt bad for being foolish. Tom gave the lamp back to Mia. Mia was happy again. The lamp grew big and bright. Mia and Tom became friends and played together every day.
training: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She had an ugly lamp in her room. The lamp was big and green. She did not like the lamp. But the lamp was a gift from her grandma, so she kept it. One day, Mia found a button on the lamp. She pushed it, and the lamp started to talk! The lamp could record what Mia said. Mia was very happy. She talked to the lamp every day. She told the lamp stories and sang songs. One day, Mia's grandma came to visit. Mia showed her the talking lamp. Grandma smiled and said, "I knew you would find the button." Mia and her grandma talked and sang with the lamp together. Mia now loved her ugly lamp.

validation: Mama was in the kitchen getting dinner ready. Baby wanted to help, but Mama said no. "Mama, can I do something?" asked Baby. "No, Baby. You need to stay out," Mama said. Baby saw a big black box sitting in the corner. It had a fierce look. "Mama, what's in the box?" Baby asked. Mama sighed. "It's just some old things, Baby. You can't touch it," she said. But Baby was curious. He wanted to see what was inside. He moved closer. "No, Baby!" Mama said. "You mustn't remove things from the box!" Baby stepped back. He didn't want to make Mama mad. Mama smiled at him. "Now stay out of trouble, okay?" Baby nodded. He stayed far away from the black box.
training: Once upon a time, there was a mama and a baby. Mama and the baby wanted to stay together, but Mama needed to go away. The baby was very sad and wanted Mama to stay. Mama tried to give the baby a yummy treat, but the baby still wanted Mama to stay. So Mama started to weep, and the baby said, "Mama, don't cry, you can stay." Mama was so happy, so she gave the baby an extra big hug and kiss. After that, the baby and Mama stayed together and were very, very happy!

validation: Ben is a boy who likes to dig in the dirt. He has a shovel and a bucket. He digs and digs and finds many things. He finds rocks and worms and roots. He is happy. One day, he digs and finds something new. It is brown and furry and has a long nose. It is a mole. The mole is scared of Ben. It tries to run away. Ben is curious. He wants to see the mole. He puts the mole in his bucket and covers it with dirt. He thinks the mole will be his friend. He takes the bucket to his house. He shows the mole to his mom and dad. They are not happy. They say the mole belongs in the dirt. They say the mole is not a pet. Ben is sad. He likes the mole. He thinks the mole is clever. He thinks the mole can dig better than him. He wants to play with the mole. He does not want to let the mole go. But he sees the mole is not happy. The mole is scared and lonely. The mole wants to go back to the dirt. The mole wants to be free. Ben understands. He loves the mole. He wants the mole to be happy. He takes the bucket to the garden. He digs a hole and puts the mole in it. He says goodbye to the mole. He hopes the mole will find his family and friends. He hopes the mole will remember him. He smiles and waves. The mole pops his head out and winks. He is clever. He is grateful. He is free.
training: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the garden. One day, she saw a mole digging a hole in the ground. She recognized the mole because she had seen one before in a book. Lily wanted to say hello to the mole, but the mole didn't hear her. So, Lily started to sing a song. The mole popped his head out of the hole and looked at Lily. Lily thought the mole was cute, but the mole thought Lily was rude for interrupting his work. Lily apologized to the mole and they became friends. They played together in the garden every day. The mole showed Lily how to dig a hole and Lily showed the mole how to sing a song. They had lots of fun together and never forgot their first meeting.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sun. One day, Lily saw a lizard on the ground. The lizard was green and had a long tail. Lily wanted to say hello to the lizard, but she was scared it might hurt her. Lily went to get a cup of water to drink. She was thirsty because playing outside made her hot. When she came back to the lizard, she saw that it was still there. Lily poured some water on the ground next to the lizard. The lizard drank the water and looked happy. Lily realized that the lizard was not going to hurt her. She got closer and said hello. The lizard looked at her with its big eyes and then ran away. Lily felt happy that she made a new friend.
training: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she found a lizard hiding under a rock. The lizard was green and had a long tail. Lily picked up the lizard very carefully because she knew it was fragile and could break easily. She held the lizard gently in her hands and looked at it closely. The lizard looked back at her with its big eyes. Lily decided to include the lizard in her game. She made a little house for the lizard out of leaves and twigs. The lizard seemed happy in its new home. Lily was happy too because she had made a new friend. From that day on, Lily always looked for the lizard when she played in the garden.

validation: Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were walking in the woods when they saw a turkey. "Let's get the turkey!" said Jack. Jill was scared so she said, "No. That turkey is too fast. We won't be able to get it." Jack didn't give up and said, "I can get the turkey if I run fast." Jack ran fast, but the turkey ran faster. Then something amazing happened. Jack received help from a friendly animal! The animal ran after the turkey and caught it. Jack was very happy and said, "Thank you for helping me get the turkey." The animal smiled and said, "You're welcome. Now you can enjoy the turkey. Have a good day!" Jack and Jill received the turkey and ran home. They had a wonderful dinner that day and were very happy.
training: Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big turkey on the grass. The turkey had brown and white feathers and a red thing on its head. "Look, a turkey!" Anna said. "Let's go and say hello." They ran to the turkey and smiled. The turkey looked at them and made a loud noise. "Gobble, gobble!" "Hi, turkey!" Ben said. "Do you want to play with us?" The turkey nodded and followed them. They showed the turkey their toys and games. The turkey liked to spin the ball and the hoop. He also liked to chase the bubbles and the leaves. "You are a good turkey," Anna said. "You are fun and friendly." The turkey was happy. He spun around and flapped his wings. He gave Anna and Ben a hug. "Gobble, gobble!" They played until it was time to go home. They said goodbye to the turkey and thanked him for playing. The turkey waved and smiled. He hoped to see them again.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a kangaroo named Joey. Joey was a big kangaroo who liked to hop and play all day. One day, Joey got lost in the forest and he was confused. He didn't know which way to go to find his way back home. Joey sat down and started to plan. He thought about the way he came and tried to remember the trees and bushes he saw. After a while, Joey figured out the right way and started to hop towards home. When Joey finally made it back home, all his kangaroo friends were so happy to see him. They asked him where he had been and Joey explained that he got lost but he made a plan to find his way back. From that day on, Joey was known as the smartest kangaroo in the forest.
training: Once upon a time, there was a kangaroo named Joey. Joey was an adventurous kangaroo who loved to hop and explore. One day, Joey met a little girl named Lily. "Hi there, Joey!" Lily said. "What are you doing?" "I'm exploring," Joey explained. "I like to see new things." Lily smiled. "Can I explore with you?" "Sure!" Joey said. "Hop on my back!" Together, Joey and Lily hopped through the forest. They saw tall trees, colorful flowers, and even a little stream. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a bear! Joey knew just what to do. He hopped quickly away, with Lily holding on tight. "Thank you, Joey," Lily said. "You're a very brave kangaroo." Joey smiled. "I'm just an adventurous kangaroo who likes to help his friends."

validation: Once upon a time, there was a purple hedge. It was a big hedge that lived in a garden. One night, the moon came out and the hedge started to glow. It looked very pretty! The hedge was happy because it had never glowed before. The little animals in the garden saw the glowing hedge and they were amazed. They all gathered around the hedge and danced. The hedge felt loved and happy. From that day on, the hedge would glow every night and the animals would come and dance with it. The end.
training: Tom and Lily are playing in the garden. They like to run and jump and hide behind the hedge. The hedge is big and green and has many flowers. Sometimes they see birds and bees and butterflies near the hedge. One day, they see a big truck come to the garden. The truck has a loud noise and a big arm. The arm has a claw that can grab things. Tom and Lily are curious and scared. They run to their mom and ask her what is happening. Mom says, "The truck is here to remove the hedge. The hedge is old and sick and needs to go. We will plant a new hedge soon. Don't worry, my loves." Tom and Lily are sad. They like the hedge. They say, "But mom, the hedge is our friend. It has flowers and animals and makes us happy. Can we keep the hedge, please?" Mom hugs them and says, "I know, my loves, but the hedge is not happy. It is hurting and dying and needs to rest. We can keep some flowers and make a bouquet. We can also make a bird feeder and a butterfly house for the new hedge. The new hedge will be white and beautiful and will grow fast. You will make new friends with the new hedge, I promise." Tom and Lily are still sad, but they understand. They say goodbye to the hedge and thank it for the fun times. They help mom pick some flowers and make a bouquet. They watch the truck remove the hedge and leave a big space. They hope the new hedge will come soon and be nice. They hug mom and go inside for a snack.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Nutty. Nutty loved to play and eat acorns. One day, Nutty found a big oak tree with lots of yummy acorns. Nutty ate and ate until he was full. But he didn't stop there. Nutty kept eating and eating until he couldn't eat anymore. The next day, Nutty went back to the oak tree, but all the acorns were gone. Nutty realized that he had eaten all the acorns and didn't leave any for the other animals. Nutty felt very spoiled and greedy. He knew he had to make things right. So, Nutty started to pack all the acorns he could find and brought them to the other animals. The animals were very happy and thanked Nutty for sharing. Nutty realized that it feels good to share and not be spoiled. From that day on, Nutty always shared his acorns with the other animals and they all lived happily ever after.
training: Once upon a time, there was a squirrel named Nutty. Nutty loved to play in the park and collect acorns. One day, Nutty was running around and saw a clear path. He ran down the path and found a big pile of acorns. Nutty was so happy! Suddenly, Nutty heard a loud noise. It was a car coming down the road. Nutty knew he had to stop and wait for the car to pass. After the car passed, Nutty continued to play and collect acorns. He was so happy to have a clear path to run on and find more acorns.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite toy, a teddy bear, that she loved to play with every day. One Tuesday, when she was playing with her teddy bear, she accidentally dropped it and it broke. Lily was very sad and cried a lot. Her mom came into the room and saw her crying. "What happened, Lily?" she asked. "My teddy bear is broken," Lily replied. Her mom tried to fix the teddy bear, but it was too broken to be fixed. "I'm sorry, Lily. We'll have to get you a new teddy bear," her mom said. Lily was happy to hear that she would get a new teddy bear, but she was still sad that her old one was broken. The next day, her mom appeared with a new teddy bear and Lily was very happy. She hugged her new teddy bear and said, "Thank you, Mommy. I love my new teddy bear."
training: Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite teddy bear that she carried everywhere with her. One day, Lily noticed that her teddy bear was getting old and worn out. She said to her mom, "Teddy is old. Can we replace him?" Her mom said, "Sure, we can get you a new teddy bear." They went to the store and picked out a new teddy bear that was soft and gray. Lily was happy to have a new friend to play with. That night, Lily went to bed with her new teddy bear. She noticed that the room was quiet and dark. She whispered to her teddy bear, "I don't like it when it's quiet. Can you talk to me?" The teddy bear didn't say anything, but Lily felt comforted just having him there. She fell asleep with a smile on her face, happy to have a new friend and a cozy room.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to eat. One day, Kitty wanted to order a big meal. At night, Kitty went to the store. But the store was closed. But then, Kitty found a big cake. Kitty ate the cake and was happy again.
training: Once upon a time, there was a small cat named Kitty. Kitty liked to play with her friends, but sometimes she was not nice. One day, Kitty took her friend's toy without asking. Kitty's friend, Doggy, said, "Kitty, that's my toy! Please give it back!" But Kitty didn't want to give it back. She ran away with the toy and hid it under a tree. One day, the animals caught Kitty taking another toy. They said, "Now you must go to jail." They put Kitty in a small jail made of sticks. Kitty was sad, and she did not like the bad ending. validation: One day, a boy named Tim found an unusual tray. It had many colors and shapes on it. He showed it to his mom. "Look, mom! I found a tray!" he said. His mom looked at the tray and said, "That is an unusual tray, Tim. Be careful with it." Tim took the tray to his room and played with it. He put his toys on the tray and carried them around. Tim's friend, Sam, came over to play. Sam saw the tray and wanted to play with it too. But Tim did not want to share. "No, Sam! This is my tray!" he said. Sam got sad and quit playing with Tim. Because Tim did not share the unusual tray, Sam went home. Tim's mom was not happy with him. She took the tray away and told Tim, "You must learn to share." Tim was sad and alone, wishing he had shared the unusual tray with Sam.
training: Once upon a time, there was a large tray. The tray was made of wood, and it was very strong. One day, the tray was put up in the air and it was hung on the wall. The sister hung her schoolbag and the brother hung his toys. Everyone had something special on the large tray. The tray even had room for snacks. The mom put some apples and oranges on the tray, so they were easy to reach. The family loved the hanging tray, and they all grabbed snacks from it every day. The large tray kept everybody happy. It was a special part of the family. Everyone loved having the tray hang in their home.

validation: Ben had a parrot named Polly. Polly was a good parrot. She could talk and sing and make funny noises. Ben loved Polly very much. One day, Ben and Polly were playing in the backyard. Ben threw a ball and Polly flew after it. But Polly flew too fast and hit a tree. Polly fell to the ground and cried. Ben ran to Polly and picked her up. "Polly, are you okay?" Ben asked. He saw that Polly had a cut on her wing. It was red and hurt. Ben felt sad and scared. "Polly hurt, Polly hurt!" Polly said. She was in pain and scared too. Ben hugged Polly and said, "Don't worry, Polly. I will help you. We will go to the vet. The vet will make you better. You are my best friend, Polly. I love you." Ben took Polly inside and told his mom what happened. His mom said, "Oh, poor Polly. Let's go to the vet right away. He will fix Polly's wing. You are a good boy, Ben. You care for Polly." Ben and his mom got in the car and drove to the vet. The vet was a nice man. He looked at Polly's wing and said, "Polly has a small cut. It is not bad. I will clean it and put a bandage on it. Polly will be fine. She just needs some rest and love." The vet cleaned Polly's wing and put a bandage on it. He gave Polly a treat and said, "You are a brave parrot, Polly. You will heal soon. You have a good friend, Ben. He loves you." Polly smiled and said, "Thank you, vet. Thank you, Ben. I love you too." Ben and his mom took Polly home. Ben put Polly in her cage and gave her some water and food. He said, "Polly, you are my best friend. I am sorry you got hurt. I will never quit playing with you. I will always be with you." Polly said, "Ben, you are my best friend too. I am happy you helped me. I will never quit talking to you. I will always love you."
training: Once upon a time, there was a parrot named Polly. Polly was very healthy because she ate lots of fruits and veggies. One day, Polly saw a man who wanted to buy her. The man said, "I want to take you home with me, Polly. You can be my pet." Polly didn't want to go with the man, so she signed with her wings and said, "No, thank you. I like living here in the jungle with my friends." The man was sad, but he understood what Polly wanted. From that day on, Polly lived happily in the jungle with her friends, eating healthy foods and signing with her wings whenever someone wanted to take her away.

training: Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved ice cream more than anything in the world. One day, Timmy went to the store with his mom to buy some ice cream. Timmy and his mom tried the ice cream and it was delicious! They were so happy they found a cheaper option that tasted just as good.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a fish who loved the sea. Whenever the fish swam near the surface of the water, they saw a big, scary shark. training: Once upon a time, there was a deaf shark. She liked to swim and bounce around in the ocean. One day, she saw a little fish with big red eyes. The little fish said to the shark, "Will you play with me?" The shark happily said yes and together they started to bounce in the sea. First, the fish and the shark bounced around big rocks. Then, the shark leapt over the fish and made a big splash. The little fish laughed and clapped his fins. Next, the shark raced the fish to the coral reef. She was so fast she beat the fish and reached the reef first! Finally, the shark and the fish swam together for hours. They were having so much fun! After a while, the sun started to set and the sky turned blue and pink. The fish and shark said goodbye and the shark swam back home. And they all lived happily ever after.

validation: Once upon a time, there was a famous duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond and quack with his friends. One day, Ducky met a little girl who wanted to play with him. validation: Once upon a time, there was a jolly motor. The motor hummed and whirred and it churned away, day after day. One day, a little boy was so excited when he saw the motor.
